desc:
Custom native modules for React Native apps give your JavaScript code access to phone features it cannot reach alone. Ecom Swift LLC writes the Swift and Kotlin code, wraps it with typed methods and delivers an example screen, notes and device tests.

## What is a React Native native module?

A native module is a piece of Swift, Objective-C, Kotlin or Java code that your React Native app can call from JavaScript. It acts as a bridge. Your screen calls a simple function, and the module talks to the phone's own system, then sends back a result or an event.

Most apps never need one, because libraries already cover cameras, maps and storage. You need a custom module when a feature has no suitable library, or when a library is outdated or incomplete.

## Why do some features need native code?

JavaScript runs inside the app, but it cannot reach every part of the phone. Bluetooth accessories, home screen widgets, background services, custom camera processing and vendor SDKs for payment terminals or health devices often expose only a native interface.

Without a proper bridge, teams use workarounds that break on updates or crash on one platform. A clean module isolates the platform-specific code in one place, so the rest of your app stays simple and shared.

## How a good module affects stability and future work

The quality of a module shows up in small details. Does it ask for permission at the right moment? Does it handle a device that is switched off? Does it release resources when the screen closes? Gaps here cause the crashes that users blame on the whole app.

A typed, documented module also saves time later. Another developer can call it without reading Swift or Kotlin, and you can reuse it in another app. Cost and effort depend on the SDK or device involved, so we confirm the scope after reading its documentation.

## What a solid native module includes

- Native code in Swift for iOS and Kotlin for Android, written in clear, small files.
- Typed JavaScript or TypeScript methods that match the native behavior.
- Events sent from the phone back to your JavaScript code.
- Permission requests and denied-permission handling.
- Error messages that explain what failed and what the user can do.
- Wrapping of a third-party SDK so your app never touches it directly.
- An optional native view component for custom interface elements.
- An example screen that proves the module works.
- Unit tests for the native code and trials on real devices.
- Setup notes and a developer guide for your team.

## What we do

We start by reading the SDK or device documentation and agreeing a list of methods and events in plain language. You approve that list, which becomes the contract between your app and the module.

Then we write the native code and the JavaScript layer, build an example screen and test on real hardware. Basic delivers one module on one platform. Standard covers both platforms with events, permissions and error handling. Premium covers up to two modules or one module with a native view, a wrapped third-party SDK, native tests and a handover call. We also check that it works with current React Native releases.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share the SDK documentation, sample code and any test hardware details.
- Decide which methods the JavaScript side really needs.
- Tell us which platforms and OS levels you must support.
- Test the module on at least one real device from each platform.
- Keep the module in its own folder or package.

**Avoid:**
- Writing native code for something a maintained library already does.
- Exposing every native function when the app only needs a few.
- Ignoring permission denials and background behavior.
- Mixing app logic into the native layer.
- Assuming a simulator can test hardware features.

## Who this service is for

A product team connecting an app to a Bluetooth device or sensor. A company with a vendor SDK that only ships native code. A developer who needs a widget, a custom camera step or a background task and does not write Swift or Kotlin.

## What we need from you

The SDK or documentation, a short description of what the module must do and repository access as a collaborator. If the feature needs special hardware, tell us early. We never need your passwords, and any vendor keys are handled through test accounts or secure sharing.
